correctness.rationale: Verified the fixed-tree proof in RESULT.md lines 40–55. A queried edge witnesses its own empty singleton trace, and in a tree with ≥2 edges it has a neighbor. For a support of two edges incident at u, the two own-edge witnesses realize the singleton traces, an extra edge at u is required for the full trace, and the empty trace requires either a second edge in an unchosen branch or a third edge in any branch. When no branch extends three edges, precisely those pairs containing every depth-two branch fail the empty-trace condition, giving B_u. For a disjoint pair, the middle edge of their unique three-edge connecting path is the only possible joint witness, and another edge is needed at an endpoint of each outer edge for each singleton, giving the two degree-sum tests. Any all-support witness splits the support among its endpoints. For a mixed support of size ≥3, choosing one edge from each side gives a disjoint pair whose only common neighbor is the all-support witness, so the pair trace is missing. The remaining triples are stars: the omitted support edge gives each doubleton, each singleton requires extension on its chosen branch, and the same branch test gives the empty trace. Four-edge stars have no two-element trace, excluding them and all larger supports by heredity. Eight distinct witnesses are necessary for a shattered triple; the four length-two arms supply them on nine vertices and give four shattered triples. The attached Prüfer verifier was inspected, not executed; the separately reported unlabeled census is corroboration only.

evidence: 3519bee5e97b states the maximal open-neighborhood trace count for block graphs is 2^m for m≤3 and 3m−2 for m≥4. Tree line graphs are block graphs.
The rank-width-one record bounds the four-point profile by 12; the Johnson-graph source gives VC dimension at most four for induced subgraphs, including tree line graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The block-graph bound is genuine implication coverage of no four-point shattering here. It does not count how many two- or three-supports of any fixed tree attain the full trace set, nor give the first such tree order. The earlier Johnson bound is weaker.

evidence: A class maximum of eight traces on three points says neither which individual trees achieve eight nor how many supports in them do so.

value.rationale: The exact per-tree census gives structural information not furnished by a sharp class maximum: it identifies separate depth-two and depth-three branch effects and counts supports for every tree without enumerating all witnesses against all supports. The nine-vertex witness and counting lower bound fix a meaningful first occurrence of the top-degree term. The result is restricted to open line-graph neighborhoods with internal witnesses allowed.
